tutorial.title: How to play BlaBlind
tutorial.subtitle: Create your account, set up a game, invite your friends, buzz. The full tour in a few minutes.
tutorial.intro: BlaBlind is a music blindtest played together, live, from any browser. Nothing to install. Start by creating an account: it's what lets you prepare your evenings, keep the tracks you discover and find your past games. Your guests only need to type a nickname to join you.
tutorial.cta_title: Ready to start your first game?
tutorial.account_intro: Two minutes, and everything else gets easier: playlists ready in advance, the tracks you set aside at the end of a game, your default game settings and the history of your evenings.
tutorial.account_1_text: The "Login" button at the top of the screen opens the login window. Under the form, the "Sign up" link switches over to creating an account.
tutorial.account_2_text: A name, an email, a password of at least eight characters. The name is the one shown during games — you can change it later from your profile. You then get a confirmation email: the link inside activates the account.
tutorial.account_tip: You can absolutely play without an account, and guests are full players: they score, they appear in the standings, and they add their tracks like anyone else. An account is for preparing, not for taking part.
tutorial.create_intro: Whoever is hosting the evening creates the session. It's the only step that asks for a few settings — everything else is built together with the other players.
tutorial.create_1_text: On the home page, the "Create a blindtest" button opens a wizard that asks one question at a time. Next to it, the "Join" field is how you enter an existing game once someone has given you its code.
tutorial.create_2_text: In Classic mode, each player adds their own tracks during the game, and whoever added a track validates the others' answers to it. In Autonomous mode, the game runs off a playlist prepared in advance: nobody plays game master, and answers are validated by a vote among the other players. Autonomous mode needs at least three players for the votes to mean anything.
tutorial.create_3_text: That name doubles as the address: it becomes the link you'll share. Pick something your friends will recognise.
tutorial.create_4_text: The wizard then walks through the rules: how many attempts per track, how long before you may buzz again, how long the validator has before an answer is auto-rejected, and whether the music keeps playing after a correct answer. All of it stays editable mid-game from the room menu.
tutorial.create_tip: Nothing is set in stone: reopen the settings during the game if a rule isn't working out.
tutorial.invite_intro: Once the session exists you land in the waiting room. That's where everyone gathers before the first track.
tutorial.invite_1_title: Share the link or QR code
tutorial.invite_1_text: In the room menu, "Share the blindtest" shows a QR code to scan and a link to copy. In person the QR code is fastest: everyone scans it and lands straight in the room.
tutorial.invite_2_text: Opening the link, a new player only has to type a nickname. No account, no email, no app. Their identity is kept in their browser: if they reload the page or lose signal, they come back to the game with their score intact.
tutorial.invite_3_text: You watch players arrive live, and see who is ready. The blindtest can only start once at least one track has been added.
tutorial.invite_4_text: Every player adds the tracks they want the others to guess. The search looks in BlaBlind's own library first — everything previous games have left there — and falls back to YouTube by itself when it finds nothing. For each track you choose which second the excerpt starts at, how long it plays, and when the answer is revealed. You can also paste a YouTube URL directly, or pull from your favourites.
tutorial.invite_tip: The tracks you add stay hidden from everyone but you: you can't score on them, but you see their title so you can validate the answers.
tutorial.play_intro: By default a BlaBlind game is played in one room: a single device plays the music, everyone hears it, and answers are called out loud. That's IRL mode, marked by the orange badge at the top of the room.
tutorial.play_1_text: The current track stays hidden: all you see is who added it, and whose device is playing it. Below, the buzz button spans the full width — it's the only gesture you need. The tabs then list upcoming tracks, the ones already played with their answer, and the live standings.
tutorial.play_2_text: Two separate roles, and not necessarily the same person. The host coordinates the game; the DJ is whoever's device plays the music — usually the one plugged into the speaker. From the menu, “Host & DJ” shows who holds what, and “Become DJ” asks to take over: the current DJ accepts or declines. Handy when a battery gives out.
tutorial.play_3_text: One big button, one gesture: in IRL mode, buzzing raises your hand straight away, with nothing to type. The screen confirms it with “Your turn to answer!”, the music pauses, and you call out your answer. Get it wrong and you can try again after the rebuzz delay, within the number of attempts allowed.
tutorial.play_4_text: The player who added the track sees who buzzed and rules on what they just heard: right or wrong. Nothing is written on screen — they are the referee. If they don't react, the answer is automatically rejected after the configured delay and the game moves on.
tutorial.play_5_text: The score isn't a plain point counter: it's your share of correct answers among the tracks you could actually guess, meaning every track you didn't add yourself. Nobody is penalised for bringing more music than the others.
tutorial.play_tip: Playing remotely? Switch IRL mode off from the menu: everyone then listens on their own device and types their answer instead of saying it. Either way, keep the screens awake — the host's device is what advances the tracks, and the DJ's is what plays the music. A phone that locks itself stalls the game for everyone.
tutorial.member_intro: Once you're logged in, your area gathers everything you prepare between two evenings.
tutorial.member_1_text: Your member area opens on your profile: the name shown in games, your avatar, and a summary of your activity.
tutorial.member_2_text: The list of your games, both the ones you created and the ones you joined. Reopen any of them to look back at the tracks played and the scores.
tutorial.member_3_text: A playlist is a blindtest prepared in advance: tracks stored with their timings already dialled in. It's what feeds autonomous mode, where there is no game master to add music on the fly.
tutorial.member_4_text: For each track you adjust the start point, the length of the excerpt and the reveal moment, and you can listen to the result before saving. Reorder by dragging.
tutorial.member_5_text: Tracks you set aside at the end of a game land here, along with the name of the person who introduced you to them. It's your stock for building the next playlist.
tutorial.member_6_text: The settings you define here become the defaults for the blindtests you create. No need to walk through the whole wizard every evening.
tutorial.member_tip: A playlist marked public is visible to other members, who can use it for their own blindtests.
tutorial.invite_5_text: When the library has answered but your track isn't in it, the “Search on YouTube too” button under the results casts a wider net. Both lists are deliberately short: ten results from YouTube, twenty from the library. If you still can't find what you're after, refine the search rather than run it again — add the artist, pin down the title.
tutorial.play_6_text: The podium appears, followed by the full list of tracks played. A star next to each one adds it to your favourites so you can reuse it in a later game.
